title: Distributed Keystore Convergence Plan — v0.1 (sketch)
body:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a converged plan to migrate several existing secret storage patterns into a unified distributed keystore abstraction for private deployments (VPC + on-prem). Target is to enable HSM-backed keys where available, seamless KMS proxy fallback, explicit audit trails, and a Terraform-friendly module graph for staged upgrades.

Goals (measurable):
- Replace ad-hoc secret sidecars in customer manifests with a single keystore operator within 6 months for new installs.
- Ensure HSM-backed key usage for >= 80% of production tenants that opt in, with attested key usage telemetry.
- Provide terraform module upgrades that preserve on-disk state and minimize downtime (target: <5m per node group).
- Emit immutable audit events to customer-configured logging endpoints (S3/ELK/syslog) and Redwood control-plane audit (opt-in).

Non-goals:
- Fixing application-level secret formats (apps should adopt secret wrapper shim in a follow-up).
- Replacing customer-managed KMS solutions – we provide adapters.

High-level architecture (converged):
- Keystore operator: Kubernetes operator that coordinates local keystore instances per node-pool and exposes a gRPC endpoint on a secure loopback for sidecars.
- Keystore instances: thin local process managing key material, interfacing to either: (a) cloud KMS via authenticated mTLS proxies, (b) an HSM (PKCS#11) using an HSM agent, or (c) a file-backed software keystore for dev-only.
- KMS proxy: short-lived token exchange service that mediates between keystore and remote KMS; supports fallback policies and rate-limit throttles.
- Audit-forwarder: component that signs and forwards audit events (key-create, wrap/unwrap, usage) with sequence numbers to a customer sink and to an immutable append-only ledger (optional).

Terraform module notes (developer-facing):
- Modules to add/upgrade: module.keystore.operator (v0.1), module.keystore.hsm_adapter (v0.1), module.keystore.kms_proxy (v0.1), module.keystore.audit (v0.1).
- State handling: operator state is intentionally mostly off-cluster (object references in Terraform), but node-level key metadata lives in a Consul/etcd KV (configurable). We MUST avoid storing raw keys in TF state; state tables must be marked as sensitive and mostly metadata-only.
- Versioning policy: each module includes a schema migration function (terraform external data script) that can map old resource ids to new ones. Bump major for any breaking naming changes.
- Example variable schema (summary):
  - keystore.mode: ["hsm","kms-proxy","local"]
  - hsm.pkcs11_lib_path: string (optional)
  - kms.endpoint: string
  - audit.endpoint: string
  - fallback.policy: ["prefer-hsm","fallback-to-kms","strict"]
- Recommended provider constraints: require terraform >= 1.5, provider.kubernetes >= 2.11, provider.external >= 2.2.

Upgrade/migration plan (phased):
Phase 0 — preflight (manual checks)
- Validate HSM firmware + drivers on target hosts (run hsm-check.sh).
- Inventory existing secret sidecars and KMS integrations (run discovery job; outputs csv).
- Verify TLS PKI distribution across cluster (cert validity, SANs).

Phase 1 — install keystore operator in read-only mode
- Deploy operator with mode=read-only; it will watch resources and surface drift but not rotate or create keys.
- Run compatibility analyzer (terraform external) to produce a migration map (old_secret_id -> keystore_alias).
- Smoke tests: ensure operator can read metadata and list keys (no unseal).

Phase 2 — enable HSM adapters (opt-in per node-pool)
- Roll out hsm_adapter as a DaemonSet with PKCS#11 path mounted into a sealed filesystem.
- For nodes with proven attestation, set keystore.mode=hsm and create a test encrypted token that must be unwrapped by HSM.
- Verify attestation certificates and telemetry.

Phase 3 — promote to active + traffic migration
- Switch small percentage (canary) of workloads to use the operator's gRPC endpoint for unwrap operations.
- Monitor latency, errors, and audit events for 48–72h.
- If success, increase percentage gradually.

Phase 4 — state cleanup and deprecation
- After all workloads migrated, run automated cleanup to remove legacy sidecar secrets (preserving a 30d retention).
- Provide an undo plan that can re-register prior secret ids into legacy consumer mode for rollback.

Operational runbook (concise):
- Key compromise scenario: immediate rotation via operator API -> create new DEK, rewrap existing ciphertexts, push rollout plan to applications via config map updates.
- HSM failover: operator detects PKCS#11 errors -> promote node to "locked" state and redirect unwrap requests to kms-proxy; emit high-sev alert.
- Audit discrepancy: if forwarder detects non-monotonic sequence numbers, freeze key operations and trigger manual reconciliation.

Audit logging and observability:
- Events to emit: KEY_CREATE, KEY_ROTATE, KEY_WRAP, KEY_UNWRAP, ACL_CHANGE, AUDIT_FORWARD_FAILURE.
- Logs must include: timestamp (RFC3339), keystore_alias, operation_id (uuid), caller_identity (mTLS cert CN or token actor), result code, duration_ms, node_id, optional trace_id.
- Audit sink adapters: s3, elasticsearch, syslog, splunk; each adapter supports TLS+mutual auth and batching with guaranteed-at-least-once delivery semantics.
- Metric set: keystore.ops_total{op="unwrap|wrap|rotate"}, keystore.op_latency_ms_p50/p90/p99, keystore.audit_forward_failures_total.

Testing & validation checklist (pre-merge):
- Unit tests for terraform module variable schema and terraform plan diffs.
- Integration harness: a k3s cluster with simulated HSM using SoftHSM2 and a mock KMS endpoint. Run a full migration test that: creates secrets in legacy sidecar mode, migrates metadata, flips consumer to operator endpoint, validates decrypts succeed.
- Chaos tests: kill HSM adapter process mid-unlock and assert fallback to KMS proxy occurs within timeout.
- Performance baseline: unwrap p50 < 15ms for soft-hsm, < 5ms for HSM, with 95% success under 500 concurrent sessions (workload dependent).

Security considerations & threat model notes: 
- Attestation: use TPM-based node attestation or cloud provider instance identity to assert HSM presence. Store attestation certs in a short-lived provisioning CA.
- Least privilege: operator uses distinct service accounts for node-level operations vs cluster admin tasks; use Kubernetes RBAC constraints with explicit rolebindings per namespace.
- Secret-in-transit: gRPC between sidecars and keystore uses mTLS with pinned CA; support optional mutual-auth with SPIFFE identities.
- Secret-at-rest: never persist raw DEKs to Terraform state or object storage. Where unavoidable use envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS.
- Tamper evidence: audit-forwarder signs batches with an append-only ledger root hash and optionally publishes to customer ledger endpoint for verification.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Do we require HSM in all production clusters or allow per-customer opt-in? (recommending opt-in for now)
- Support for off-cluster KMS via private link — how to validate latency/SLOs and design quotas?
- How aggressive should automated rotation be versus operator-triggered rotation?

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Build PoC terraform module (module.keystore.operator) and validate no TF state captures key material (Assignee: Marco).
- Create integration harness repo with SoftHSM tests (Assignee: Zoe).
- Draft external API for operator (gRPC proto + minimal REST admin) and circulate for review (Assignee: Aisha).
- Schedule migration pilot with 1 customer in staging (Ops lead to coordinate).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a high-level convergence plan. Expect several follow-up artifacts: detailed terraform upgrade scripts, operator design doc with sequence diagrams, and attestation CA lifecycle playbook.
- I left some concrete command snippets out until we align on the migration map format; happy to add examples in a follow-up.

Appendix: quick reference commands (examples)
- hsm-check.sh --run --node node-12 (verifies driver + pkcs11 accessible)
- terraform -chdir=infra/keystore apply -var-file=secrets.tfvars --target=module.keystore.hsm_adapter
- curl -XPOST https://operator.local/admin/v1/rotate -d '{"alias":"app/foo"}' --cert client.pem

End of sketch.
